title: Crispy Honey Chili Sausage
subtitle: English breakfast components roasted and finished on one pan.
description: Adapted from classic full English breakfast tradition for firehall batch service: bacon, sausages, baked beans, roasted tomato, and mushrooms on sheet pans, finished with fried eggs for ten crew portions.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Honey Chili Sausage in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 400°F. Line two sheet pans with foil and lightly oil. Arrange sausages on one pan and bacon on the other with space between pieces for even rendering. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Roast meats
steps.instruction: Roast sausages 15 minutes, turning once, until internal temperature reaches 160°F. Roast bacon 12–15 minutes until crisp. Hold warm tented with foil. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast veg
steps.instruction: Toss tomatoes and mushrooms with oil, salt, and pepper on a clean sheet pan. Roast at 425°F until tomatoes collapse and mushrooms brown, about 12 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Warm beans and toast
steps.instruction: Simmer baked beans in a pot over low heat, stirring occasionally. Toast bread until golden. Keep beans and toast warm on the line. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Fry eggs and assemble
steps.instruction: Fry eggs in butter over medium until whites are set (165°F) and yolks are runny. Plate each serving with sausage, bacon, beans, roasted veg, toast, and a fried egg. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Separate bacon and sausages on different pans so bacon fat does not steam the links.
Warm beans on the back burner while the oven handles veg—timing is everything.
Fry eggs in two skillets in parallel so ten plates finish within the same 5-minute window.
cleanupNotes: Drain bacon fat from foil into a container once cooled—never pour grease down the drain.
Discard foil liners with rendered fat to cut scrub time on sheet pans.
leftovers: Reheat roasted components on a sheet pan at 350°F; fry fresh eggs separately.
Mash leftover beans and sausage into a toast topping with cheddar for quick rarebit-style bites.
